logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, at phone width, a global milestone (a named group of work items) row cannot keep a long title and its repository badge separate. A long milestone title or repository name makes the badge text overlap the milestone icon/title instead of fitting or truncating within the row.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The dashboard header places a repository badge and title in the same flex row without wrapping/truncation constraints for long text. At phone width a shrinking badge/title box still paints its nowrap text across the neighboring item.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s global Milestones page at phone width, a long milestone title runs into the badge identifying its repository. The title and badge overlap instead of staying separately readable within the row.
In Gitea, at a 390px-wide viewport, a milestone row whose repository name is long shrinks the repository badge, but the badge text keeps painting past it over the milestone icon and title.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on global or organization Milestones, excluding a repository in the sidebar works until Sort > Name is chosen. That sort clears the repository selection and returns milestones (named groups of work items) from repositories the user excluded.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The Name sort URL is built separately from the other sort links and omits repos. Both global and organization dashboards share this template, so excluded repository milestones return.
reproductionPaths: On Gitea’s global Milestones page, exclude a repository using the sidebar selection and then choose Sort > Name. Milestones from the excluded repository reappear because changing that sort discards the repository selection.

On a Gitea organization's Milestones page, after excluding a repository with the sidebar filter, choosing Sort > Name brings the excluded repository's milestones back. The Name sort link doesn't carry the selected repositories.

logicalBugs.description: A Gitea milestone groups related work items under a title and optional target date. On the milestone list, submitting a search drops the chosen Latest due date sort, so the matching milestones no longer appear in the requested date order.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The shared issue search form places its hidden sort field inside not PageIsMilestones. Milestone search thus omits sort and the handler chooses the default instead of the prior due-date ordering.
reproductionPaths: A Gitea milestone groups related work items under a title and optional target date. On the milestone list, submitting a search drops the chosen Latest due date sort, so the matching milestones no longer appear in the requested date order.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issue and milestone (a named group of work items) due dates that coincide with unset-date sentinel values, including January 1 of year 0001 or 1970, can save and remain visible in the editor but display as a dash or missing date in timeline/list views. The defect concerns an accepted date disappearing from presentation, rather than an editor rejecting it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Issue deadline comments and milestone date templates pass date-only strings through DateUtils.ParseLegacy, which reconstructs midnight in the server UI timezone. The shared anyToTime/dateTimeFormat renderer treats either Go zero time (0001-01-01 midnight in a matching timezone) or Unix timestamp 0 (1970-01-01 midnight UTC) as a missing value and prints a dash. A saved end-of-day deadline may be nonzero while this reparsed display value hits a zero sentinel; each reproduction path retains its specific date/timezone trigger.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, set a milestone’s due date to January 1, 1970 and save it. The editor retains that date, but the repository milestone list shows a dash instead of the date, so an accepted saved deadline appears absent.

A Gitea milestone due date of 0001-01-01 saves and reopens in the editor, but every milestone view shows a red calendar icon and '-' instead of the date, because the date re-parses to Go's zero time, which the date formatter treats as no date.

On Gitea’s global Milestones page (/milestones), a milestone saved with a due date of January 1, 1970 shows '-' next to the calendar icon instead of the date, with or without a search. The saved date is correct; the page treats that date as no date.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, after choosing Type > Assigned to you, switching back to All issues (tracked work items) or to another ownership type can retain the old implicit assignee restriction. Repository/milestone (a named group of work items) issue lists and organization pull request (a proposed code change) lists then omit otherwise matching records despite showing the new Type selection.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The issue handler exports the effective self assignee after Type=assigned; shared filter_list copies that AssigneeID into subsequent Type links. Created by you therefore retains an unintended assignment restriction.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea milestone’s issue list, first choose Type > Assigned to you and then switch back to All issues. Work items assigned to other users remain hidden because the previous assignment restriction is still applied despite the All issues selection.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, closing a milestone, a named group of work items, redirects to a list state that fails to display it. The page reports a closed milestone but shows no row until the user explicitly clicks Closed, which supplies the correct list-state value.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ChangeMilestoneStatus uses the action path segment as the state query. The close route therefore produces close, while the milestone list recognizes only closed; the resulting state-dependent data and controls disagree.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, closing a milestone, a named group of work items, redirects to a list state that fails to display it. The page reports a closed milestone but shows no row until the user explicitly clicks Closed, which supplies the correct list-state value.

logicalBugs.description: A Gitea milestone (a named group of work items) title made only of spaces passes the required-title check, is trimmed to an empty name, and is saved, leaving a milestone whose title link, detail heading, and picker entry are blank.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The form Required check accepts spaces; NewMilestone trims the Name only after that validation and inserts without checking the trimmed result.
reproductionPaths: A Gitea milestone title made only of spaces passes the required-title check, is trimmed to an empty name, and is saved, leaving a milestone whose title link, detail heading, and picker entry are blank.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, on SQLite, milestone search matches accented keywords with ASCII-only uppercasing, but the Open/Closed counters uppercase the keyword fully, so an accented search like café lists matching milestones (named groups of work items) under tabs that read 0 Open / 0 Closed.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Row filtering uses BuildCaseInsensitiveLike, with database case conversion, but counters compare UPPER(name) to Go strings.ToUpper(keyword). SQLite uppercases ASCII only, so accented upper/lowercase values differ between these query paths.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, on SQLite, milestone search matches accented keywords with ASCII-only uppercasing, but the Open/Closed counters uppercase the keyword fully, so an accented search like café lists matching milestones under tabs that read 0 Open / 0 Closed.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a long allowed milestone (a named group of work items) title with no spaces or hyphens does not wrap in the repository milestone list, widening the page on mobile. Opening Delete for that milestone can center confirmation on the wider layout and clip its controls beyond the phone viewport.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Repository milestone list/detail headings render the name without overflow-wrap/truncation. Their intrinsic minimum width can exceed the phone viewport, widening the page and moving viewport-centered modal controls partly out of view.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, milestone titles render without any word-break rule, so a long title with no spaces or hyphens (up to the form's 50-character limit) widens the repository milestone list and the milestone detail page past a 390px viewport, forcing horizontal scrolling.

In Gitea, an unbroken milestone title widens the repository milestone list on mobile. Its Delete confirmation can centre on the widened layout viewport, clipping the right edge and part of the Yes button beyond the visible screen.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s milestone list's Close and Open (reopen) actions redirect to the list with only a state parameter, so a search keyword and sort selected on the list are discarded and unrelated milestones (named groups of work items) reappear.
logicalBugs.rootCause: ChangeMilestoneStatus redirects with only its state parameter and does not retain q/sort from the originating list, so unrelated rows return after close/reopen.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s milestone list's Close and Open (reopen) actions redirect to the list with only a state parameter, so a search keyword and sort selected on the list are discarded and unrelated milestones reappear.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, deleting a milestone from the milestone list always redirects to the bare Milestones page, so the search keyword, sort, and Open/Closed state selected on the list are discarded and unrelated milestones (named groups of work items) reappear.
logicalBugs.rootCause: DeleteMilestone unconditionally JSONRedirects to the bare milestones route, discarding search, sorting and open/closed state.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, deleting a milestone from the milestone list always redirects to the bare Milestones page, so the search keyword, sort, and Open/Closed state selected on the list are discarded and unrelated milestones reappear.

logicalBugs.description: In a Gitea milestone’s issue (a tracked work item) list, Type > Assigned to you or Created by you overrides a later explicit Assignee or Author selection. The dropdown/URL can show nobody or another user while the results remain restricted to the signed-in user.
logicalBugs.rootCause: prepareIssueFilterAndList reads the explicit query filters, then overwrites assigneeID/posterUserID when Type is assigned/created_by. The visible independently selected filter is therefore not intersected with the ownership constraint.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, with the milestone Type filter set to Assigned to you, choosing an Assignee option such as Assigned to nobody updates the URL but leaves the list filtered only to the signed-in user, so contradictory filters show the user’s own assigned issues.

In Gitea, with the milestone Type filter set to Created by you, choosing another user in the Author filter updates the URL and shows that user as the selected Author, but the list stays filtered to the signed-in user's own issues, so contradictory filters show issues the selected author did not open.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, choosing Sort > Name on the repository or global Milestones list orders milestones (named groups of work items) in reverse alphabetical order, with no option for A to Z. Nothing breaks and the order is consistent, but a plain Name sort running Z to A is unintuitive.
logicalBugs.rootCause: FindMilestoneOptions.ToOrders maps name to name DESC and provides no ascending name alternative. The UI labels it only Name, so its Z-to-A behavior is not signaled.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, choosing Sort > Name on the repository or global Milestones list orders milestones in reverse alphabetical order, with no option for A to Z. Nothing breaks and the order is consistent, but a plain Name sort running Z to A is unintuitive.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea milestone (a named group of work items) detail page, clicking a label chip on an issue row keeps the search, Type, state and Assignee filters but drops the selected Project, Sort and Author, so the list widens to issues (tracked work items) the user had filtered out.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Issue row label links rebuild their destination from a subset of issue query parameters instead of preserving the current URL. Project, sorting and author are omitted, broadening a filtered milestone detail list.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea milestone detail page, clicking a label chip on an issue row keeps the search, Type, state and Assignee filters but drops the selected Project, Sort and Author, so the list widens to issues the user had filtered out.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issue and pull request (a proposed code change) form actions can expose a raw JSON-parsing SyntaxError labelled Network error when the server rejects an unavailable or unauthorized action. Confirmed triggers include stale deleted/locked/archived comment or issue (a tracked work item) forms, deleted milestone (a named group of work items)/time-entry targets and rejected review actions; the UI does not explain the actual refusal.
logicalBugs.rootCause: fetchActionDoRequest unconditionally calls resp.json() for HTTP 4xx and labels parsing exceptions Network error. Plain-text missing-issue/permission responses therefore expose SyntaxError rather than the rejection reason. Deleted comment inline edits use a separate parser and are kept separate.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, if the milestone selected on an unsaved New Issue draft is deleted elsewhere, clicking Create Issue shows a 'Network error SyntaxError … is not valid JSON' toast instead of saying the milestone no longer exists.

In Gitea, when a user who isn't a member or collaborator creates an issue from a public repository milestone's New Issue button, submitting fails with a red "Network error SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'N', \"Not found.\" is not valid JSON" banner, which doesn't explain what went wrong or what to do.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, issues, Pull Requests and milestone (a named group of work items) issue (a tracked work item) lists advertise Alt+Enter to exclude a label, but using that keyboard shortcut includes the label instead. Alt+click on the same label correctly applies the exclusion.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The exclusion listener is attached to the dropdown keydown, but the Fomantic keyboard path selects/activates the anchor on Enter. Its normal include navigation runs instead of the intended exclusion navigation, whereas the direct Alt+click handler sees the modifier.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea milestone's detail page, choosing a label in the Label filter with Alt+Enter includes it instead of excluding it, even though the filter's hint says Alt+click/Enter excludes labels.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, milestone title search interprets SQL wildcard characters instead of consistently searching their literal text. An underscore or bare percent can match unrelated titles, while a term beginning or ending with a literal percent can fail to find a title that contains it.
logicalBugs.rootCause: Milestone queries use LIKE through BuildCaseInsensitiveLike/builder.Like without escaping user % and _. The builder also treats leading/trailing % as an already-specified pattern rather than adding both substring wildcards, so 100% anchors at the beginning instead of finding the literal term anywhere.
reproductionPaths: In a Gitea repository or global Milestones search, enter an underscore or percent sign as literal title text. The results include titles that do not contain those characters, treating them as wildcard patterns rather than literal search terms.

Searching milestones for a term that ends (or starts) with % finds nothing even when a milestone's title contains that text: Gitea uses a search term that starts or ends with % as the raw match pattern instead of matching it anywhere in the title, so '100%' only matches titles that begin with 100. The repository, global and organization milestone lists are affected.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, a public repository's milestone (a named group of work items) page shows New Issue to users who aren't members or collaborators. The button opens a form with the milestone preselected (but shown as No Milestone and locked), and Create Issue then fails. The user should either not be offered the button or be able to create the issue (a tracked work item).
logicalBugs.rootCause: The New Issue link is outside the CanWriteIssues/CanWritePulls conditional and always includes milestone. Issue validation only permits candidate milestone IDs from authorized metadata, so a nonmember can open the advertised form but cannot submit its selected milestone.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, a public repository's milestone page shows New Issue to users who aren't members or collaborators. The button opens a form with the milestone preselected (but shown as No Milestone and locked), and Create Issue then fails. The user should either not be offered the button or be able to create the issue.

logicalBugs.description: Gitea’s New Milestone form creates a named group of work items. Clicking Create Milestone twice rapidly during the same filled-out submission can save two milestones with identical titles and descriptions, instead of treating the pending submission as one creation.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The new milestone form uses a normal submit without an in-flight submission guard or request token; NewMilestone inserts each request independently and has no deduplication boundary.
reproductionPaths: Gitea’s New Milestone form creates a named group of work items. Clicking Create Milestone twice rapidly during the same filled-out submission can save two milestones with identical titles and descriptions, instead of treating the pending submission as one creation.

logicalBugs.description: In Gitea, for an open milestone (a named group of work items) whose due date has passed, the milestone list shows the due date in red as overdue, but the milestone's own detail page shows the same date in the normal color with no overdue indication.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The detail template checks .IsOverdue and .IsClosed at the page root while the actual values belong to .Milestone. The date string is correctly read from .Milestone, but the overdue color condition remains false.
reproductionPaths: In Gitea, for an open milestone whose due date has passed, the milestone list shows the due date in red as overdue, but the milestone's own detail page shows the same date in the normal color with no overdue indication.

logicalBugs.description: On a Gitea repository's Milestones list, the default sort and Sort > Earliest due date put milestones (named groups of work items) with no due date at the top, ahead of overdue and upcoming ones, while Latest due date puts them last.
logicalBugs.rootCause: The default milestone order is deadline_unix ASC, name ASC. Missing deadlines use zero, and the ORDER BY contains no CASE/null-last handling, so undated rows precede overdue/future deadlines.
reproductionPaths: On a Gitea repository's Milestones list, the default sort and Sort > Earliest due date put milestones with no due date at the top, ahead of overdue and upcoming ones, while Latest due date puts them last.
